# library-api — the demo

A lending service for a small library: members, books, and the loans between them. Three
related entities, derived availability counts, a borrowing limit, and rules that have to
answer `409` rather than `400`.

**Every line of it was generated by Phoenix from [`spec/library.md`](spec/library.md)** — 118
lines of behavioural requirements, no code — and this build passes **51/51** of the
independent behavioural checks in [`bench/cases/library-api/checks.json`](../../bench/cases/library-api/checks.json),
driven against the booted service over HTTP by the same oracle the bench uses.

> **51/51 is one build, not a rate.** The bench measures how *often* the pipeline gets here,
> on samples drawn deliberately; a single passing build is exactly the kind of number
> [`bench/README.md`](../../bench/README.md) refuses to let anyone cite. Current measured rates
> live in [`bench/FINDINGS.md`](../../bench/FINDINGS.md). What this directory gives you is a
> real, inspectable, running artifact of the pipeline's output.

---

## Run it

```bash
cd examples/library-api
npm install
npm run dev          # → http://localhost:3000
```

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/health
# {"status":"ok","uptime":5.7}

curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/members -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ada Lovelace","email":"ada@example.com"}'
# {"id":1,"name":"Ada Lovelace","email":"ada@example.com","joined_at":"…","active_loans":0}

curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/books -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"SICP","author":"Abelson","isbn":"0-262-51087-1","copies_total":2}'
# {"id":1,…,"copies_total":2,"copies_available":2}

curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/loans -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"book_id":1,"member_id":1}'
# {"id":1,"book_id":1,"member_id":1,"borrowed_at":"…","due_at":"…14 days later…","returned_at":null}

curl -s localhost:3000/books/1
# {…,"copies_total":2,"copies_available":1}      ← derived, not stored

curl -s localhost:3000/summary
# {"members":1,"books":1,"copies_on_loan":1,"active_loans":1}
```

The interesting responses are the ones that refuse: borrowing the last copy twice is `409`,
a fourth concurrent loan for one member is `409`, a duplicate email is `409` (not `400`),
removing a member who is holding a book is `409`, and an unknown book is `404`. All of that
is in the spec as prose, and nowhere in it as code anyone wrote.

---

## The demo: five things worth showing

### 1. The routes came from the spec, not from a naming convention

```bash
grep mount src/server.ts
# mount('/books', book);
# mount('/loans', loan);
# mount('/members', member);
# mount('/summary', summary);
```

The spec's *HTTP interface* section names those paths. Until [this was
fixed](../../bench/FINDINGS.md) the mount path came from the implementation unit's name —
`/book`, `/loan` — and the app 404'd everything the spec described. The bench found it. The
interface is a contract now: `src/spec-interface.ts` matches the declared surface against
what each generated module implements, and **abstains loudly** rather than guessing.

### 2. Ask any file why it exists

```bash
npx phoenix why src/generated/loan/loan.ts
```

```
🔎 Why does src/generated/loan/loan.ts exist?

  Generated by: loan (IU 44c41635)
  Model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 · promptpack 62dfda0128d6 · 2026-08-21T17:17:26Z

  Requirements that drove this code:
    REQUIREMENT The system assigns every loan a stable unique integer identifier.
      ← spec/library.md:L35
    CONSTRAINT  The system cannot allow borrowing of a book with no available copies.
    DEFINITION  A member has at most 3 active loans at once…
    REQUIREMENT The POST /loans/:id/return endpoint returns 200 and the returned loan.
      ← spec/library.md:L57

  Provenance chain verified against 13 journal events.
```

```bash
npx phoenix journal --verify     # the chain is hash-linked; prove it
```

### 3. A formatting edit costs nothing — and does not quietly break the next one

```bash
# reindent one requirement, change its bullet, add a full stop
npx phoenix ingest
#   Re-keyed 14 canonical node(s) after 1 trivial edit(s) — provenance preserved
#   Changes: 1 clauses affected — classes 1A
#   (no invalidation line: nothing downstream is stale)
```

Class **A** is "trivial (formatting)". Nothing regenerates, nothing is marked stale, no
tokens are spent.

That `Re-keyed` line is the interesting part, and this demo is why it exists. A clause is
addressed by `sha256(doc + normalized_text)`, and the normalizer's idea of "formatting" is
narrower than the classifier's — a trailing full stop is *classified* trivial and still
changes the address. Until [this was fixed](../../src/store/canonical-store.ts), the
canonical graph kept pointing at the vanished id, and **the next real edit to that clause
invalidated nothing at all**: `phoenix ingest` said "class B" and marked zero units stale.
The defining capability, silently off, after a cosmetic edit. Now the graph follows the
address and the repair is printed and journaled.

(Regression test: `tests/e2e/selective-invalidation.test.ts` — *"a trivial edit does not
disconnect the graph from the next real one"*.)

### 4. A meaning change scopes itself

```bash
# spec/library.md: "A loan is due 14 days after it is borrowed" → 21 days
npx phoenix ingest
#   Changes: 1 clauses affected — classes 1B
#   ▸ Invalidated: 1 IU(s) stale — only these regenerate

npx phoenix status
#   Implementation Units: 4
#   Invalidation: 1 stale
#     Stale — requirements changed: spec/library.md L35 [B] → … → loan
```

One of four units is stale. `phoenix regen` regenerates that one and leaves `book`, `member`
and `summary` untouched — the PRD's defining capability, doing what it says.

**And the honest part of the same demo:** a meaning change also needs the canonical graph
re-derived, and `phoenix canonicalize` is still whole-graph today, so running it marks all
four units stale and the saving is lost:

```bash
npx phoenix canonicalize && npx phoenix regen
#   4 IU(s) regenerated.            ← not 1
grep days src/generated/loan/loan.ts
#   … datetime('now', '+21 days')   ← correct, but paid for four times
```

That gap is tracked, by name, as a known red in Phoenix's own capability suite
(`canonicalization.incremental-per-clause-not-yet-earned`, `npx phoenix selftest`). Showing
it is the point: the invalidation *scope* is already right, and the incrementality stops one
stage earlier than the marketing would like.

### 5. The trust surface tells on itself

```bash
npx phoenix status
```

This build reports **3 errors and 13 warnings** on a service that passes 51/51 behavioural
checks, and both of those statements are true:

- `book.count >= 1: no min() bound on "count"` — the spec says a copy count is "a whole number
  of at least 1". The generated module rejects `0` at the route (which is why the check
  passes) but the *declared schema* carries no `.min(1)`, so the verifier will not certify
  the rule. It is reporting a missing proof, not a missing behaviour.
- `evidence · member — Evidence failed: unit_tests` — the generated unit tests for one module
  do not pass. The app works; its own generated tests do not agree yet.
- Ten of the warnings are `normative ("must"/"never"/"only") but produced no checkable
  constraint` — spec sentences Phoenix could not turn into anything machine-checkable, listed
  rather than quietly dropped.

A dashboard that went green here would be worth less than one that says this.

## What this directory ships

Unusually for this repo, the example commits its `.phoenix/` state — the clause store, the
canonical graph, the manifests and the hash-chained journal — so that `why`, `journal
--verify`, `ingest` and selective regen all work the moment you clone, without spending a
token. Everything else here (`src/`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`) is generated output,
committed for the same reason.

## What this example is for

- **A demo** you can boot in thirty seconds and poke with `curl`.
- **A fixture with a known answer**: the same 51 checks that score it here score every arm of
  `phoenix bench`, so "does the pipeline still do this?" has a number rather than an opinion.
- **A worked example of the honest failure modes** — read `phoenix status` next to a passing
  behavioural suite and you have the whole argument of the project in one screen.

Regenerate it from scratch at any time:

```bash
rm -rf .phoenix src package.json tsconfig.json vitest.config.ts
npx phoenix init --arch=sqlite-web-api
npx phoenix bootstrap
```

The output will not be byte-identical — a model wrote it — which is why the durable assets
here are the spec and the checks, and the code is the disposable part.
